title: AFC/M23 - expansion territoriale et reconnaissance politique, selon l'ONU
excerpt: Malgré les efforts diplomatiques, le mouvement poursuit ses ambitions politiques et militaires à l'Est - avec l'idée d'une entité fédérale parallèle.
title_en: AFC/M23 Pursues Territorial Expansion and Political Recognition, UN Report Says
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 2, 2026 - The AFC/M23 armed movement continues to pursue its political and military ambitions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, despite ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the conflict and restoring stability in the region.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 2, 2026 - The AFC/M23 armed movement continues to pursue its political and military ambitions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, despite ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the conflict and restoring stability in the region.

According to a new assessment by the United Nations Group of Experts on the DRC, the movement, which controls significant areas of North Kivu and South Kivu provinces, is seeking to strengthen its territorial influence, establish parallel governance structures, and obtain official recognition through political negotiations.

The report indicates that the group’s long-term objective remains the removal of the Congolese government, while also considering the creation of an autonomous entity in eastern DRC as an alternative scenario. The movement has reportedly promoted the idea of a “Federal Republic of Congo” for territories under its control, accompanied by the establishment of its own security and defense structures.

The experts note that AFC/M23 leaders have shifted their position on the future of their fighters, moving away from previous calls for integration into the Congolese armed forces (FARDC). Instead, the group is reportedly seeking to form and lead the armed forces of a future federal entity.

The report also highlights the increasing use of narratives related to the protection of Tutsi, Banyamulenge, and Hema communities from alleged ethnic violence as part of the movement’s public justification for its military actions and political demands.

Despite international calls for the withdrawal of foreign forces and the cessation of external support to armed groups, the UN assessment states that AFC/M23 has continued expanding its areas of influence. The movement has reportedly intensified military operations with ambitions to extend its control toward strategic locations, including Walikale, Kisangani, Kalemie, and Beni.
body_fr:
Malgré les efforts diplomatiques, le mouvement poursuit ses ambitions politiques et militaires à l'Est - avec l'idée d'une entité fédérale parallèle.

title: Soudan - diplomatie et loyautés tribales redessinent les fronts de la guerre
excerpt: Après plus de trois ans de conflit, SAF et RSF ajustent alliances et stratégies - El Obeid et les corridors restent décisifs.
title_en: Diplomacy and Tribal Loyalties Redefine Sudan’s Civil War Frontlines
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 1, 2026 – More than three years into Sudan’s civil war, the conflict is increasingly being shaped by political calculations and tribal loyalties rather than military strength alone, as both the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) adjust t
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 1, 2026 – More than three years into Sudan’s civil war, the conflict is increasingly being shaped by political calculations and tribal loyalties rather than military strength alone, as both the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) adjust their strategies to changing realities on and off the battlefield.

For the Sudanese army, preserving international legitimacy has become a growing strategic priority. In recent months, the military has reduced the role of some allied armed groups whose presence has attracted international scrutiny, while strengthening cooperation with local resistance groups and former rebel movements that joined the 2020 Juba Peace Agreement.

Security analysts say the shift reflects an effort by the army to safeguard its international standing amid mounting diplomatic pressure and sanctions targeting some of its former battlefield partners. While the broader coalition has reinforced troop numbers, it has also introduced new challenges related to coordination, command structures, and operational discipline.

On the opposing side, the RSF has experienced a series of high-profile defections involving senior commanders and advisors. Although these defections have provided a political and symbolic boost to the Sudanese military, they have had only a limited impact on the military balance.

Many former RSF commanders have reportedly remained away from active combat zones after switching sides, reflecting the complex tribal and family ties that continue to connect fighters across opposing camps. Analysts note that deep-rooted kinship networks have discouraged direct confrontations between former comrades and relatives, reducing the tactical value of the defections.

As both forces reshape their alliances, the focus of the conflict has increasingly shifted toward securing strategic supply corridors, border crossings, and economically important areas rather than pursuing large-scale territorial advances.

El Obeid has become one of the war's most contested locations, with RSF forces maintaining pressure around the city while the Sudanese army continues to reinforce its defenses. The city remains a critical logistical hub linking central Sudan to the Kordofan region, making its control strategically important for both sides.

Meanwhile, fighting has intensified in South Kordofan and Blue Nile states, where the conflict now involves not only the SAF and the RSF but also the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N), creating a complex three-way confrontation.

Military observers say the war has entered a new phase in which controlling supply routes, border regions, and key economic assets has become more important than achieving decisive battlefield victories. As the conflict evolves, localized alliances and regional power dynamics are increasingly shaping the course of the war, while prospects for a comprehensive military resolution remain uncertain.

Après plus de trois ans de conflit, SAF et RSF ajustent alliances et stratégies - El Obeid et les corridors restent décisifs.

title: Présence militaire rwandaise au profit de l'AFC/M23 - l'ONU maintient l'alerte
excerpt: Un rapport onusien souligne la persistance d'un soutien militaire rwandais aux opérations de l'AFC/M23 dans l'Est congolais.
title_en: UN Report Highlights Continued Rwandan Military Presence Supporting AFC/M23 Operations
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 - The security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remains highly volatile as a United Nations assessment points to the continued presence and operational support of Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) alongside the AFC/M23 armed movement.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 - The security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remains highly volatile as a United Nations assessment points to the continued presence and operational support of Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) alongside the AFC/M23 armed movement.

The report indicates that the AFC/M23 rebellion, which maintains control over significant areas of North Kivu and South Kivu provinces, continues to benefit from military assistance that has contributed to strengthening its positions and expanding its operational capabilities across the conflict zone.

According to the assessment, thousands of RDF troops remain deployed in eastern DRC, with estimates placing their presence between 8,000 and 10,000 personnel in South Kivu and between 6,000 and 8,000 in North Kivu since late 2025. The report notes that no major withdrawal has been observed, with subsequent movements mainly involving troop rotations and reinforcements.

The document further highlights the use of advanced military capabilities, including drones, electronic warfare systems, specialized units, and other sophisticated equipment. UN experts also report that RDF elements have provided operational support to AFC/M23 forces, including assistance in offensive operations and the creation of strategic corridors.

The assessment raises concerns over RDF activities in areas where no presence of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) had been reported, including parts of Uvira territory. This development has intensified debate over Kigali’s justification that its military actions are primarily aimed at addressing security threats linked to armed groups hostile to Rwanda.

The report also describes close coordination between RDF personnel and AFC/M23 fighters, including the integration of some Rwandan units into mixed formations. It further alleges that some RDF elements adopted M23 uniforms and conducted movements mainly at night to reduce the risk of identification.

Un rapport onusien souligne la persistance d'un soutien militaire rwandais aux opérations de l'AFC/M23 dans l'Est congolais.

title: Hemetti condamné à mort par contumace pour atrocités au Darfour
excerpt: Un tribunal antiterroriste soudanais condamne le chef des RSF Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, dit Hemetti - un geste politique et judiciaire majeur.
title_en: Sudan Court Sentences RSF Leader Hemetti to Death in Absentia Over Darfur Atrocities
excerpt_en: PORT SUDAN, July 12, 2026 - A Sudanese counter-terrorism court has sentenced Rapid Support Forces (RSF) commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, widely known as Hemetti, to death in absentia, alongside two of his brothers and 13 other defendants, over crimes committed during the conflict
body_en:
PORT SUDAN, July 12, 2026 - A Sudanese counter-terrorism court has sentenced Rapid Support Forces (RSF) commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, widely known as Hemetti, to death in absentia, alongside two of his brothers and 13 other defendants, over crimes committed during the conflict in West Darfur.

The court found the defendants guilty of charges including war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide linked to the violence in El Geneina, the capital of West Darfur State.

Among the cases cited was the 2023 killing of West Darfur Governor Khamis Abakar, who was detained before being killed during intense fighting in the city.

In addition to Hemetti, the court sentenced his brothers Abdelrahim Dagalo and Al-Qoni Hamdan Dagalo, as well as several senior RSF commanders, local leaders, and individuals accused of participating in the attacks.

The court ruled that the convicted individuals were responsible for widespread attacks on civilians, destruction and looting of property, forced displacement, and assaults on residential neighbourhoods, schools, and places of worship.

Authorities also ordered the confiscation of RSF assets in favour of the Sudanese government and directed state institutions to seek international arrest notices through Interpol for the convicted individuals.

The court stated that the crimes fall under international law and are not subject to statutes of limitation or political pardons.

The violence in West Darfur during 2023 resulted in large-scale civilian casualties and forced tens of thousands of members of the Masalit community to flee across the border into eastern Chad, creating one of the conflict’s largest displacement crises.

title: Coltan de Rubaya - un réseau de contrebande organisé via le Rwanda, selon l'ONU
excerpt: L'exploitation du coltan à Rubaya s'est intensifiée. Les experts de l'ONU décrivent des circuits de contrebande structurés vers le Rwanda.
title_en: UN Report Links Rubaya Coltan to Organized Smuggling Network Through Rwanda
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 2, 2026 – The exploitation of coltan in the Rubaya mining area of North Kivu intensified significantly in 2025, with production reportedly exceeding previous estimates, according to a United Nations report detailing an organized system of mineral extraction, taxati
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 2, 2026 – The exploitation of coltan in the Rubaya mining area of North Kivu intensified significantly in 2025, with production reportedly exceeding previous estimates, according to a United Nations report detailing an organized system of mineral extraction, taxation, and cross-border trade under AFC/M23 control.

The report describes a structured revenue collection mechanism in which taxes are imposed on mineral production, with charges reportedly set at US$4 per kilogram of coltan and US$2 per kilogram of cassiterite. It also outlines a system involving licensed transporters, checkpoints, and financial channels allegedly used to collect revenues generated from the mining sector.

According to the findings, minerals extracted from Rubaya are transported through an organized supply chain before reaching companies based in Kigali, where they are processed and exported to international markets.

The report identifies Rani Mining Ltd. and Kanzamin Limited among the companies that allegedly exported substantial quantities of coltan originating from Rubaya. Customs documentation examined by investigators reportedly indicates that Rani Mining Ltd. exported more than 84 tonnes of coltan, while Kanzamin Limited exported at least 70 tonnes during 2025.

The report also points to a sharp increase in Rwanda's cassiterite exports, which reportedly rose by 58 percent, from 4,859 tonnes to 7,700 tonnes over the course of the year. According to the investigators, the increase is not consistent with Rwanda's reported domestic production levels, raising questions about the origin of the exported minerals.

As part of its investigation, the United Nations Panel of Experts requested clarification from the Rwandan government regarding these findings on April 2, 2026. At the time of the report's publication, no official response had been received.

title: Or de l'Ituri - des centaines de millions de dollars passeraient par l'Ouganda
excerpt: Selon les experts onusiens, l'or extrait en Ituri alimente des circuits illégaux vers l'Ouganda - un enjeu central de gouvernance minière.
title_en: UN Experts Estimate Hundreds of Millions of Dollars in Ituri Gold Smuggled Through Uganda
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 – Hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of gold extracted from Ituri Province is being illegally smuggled out of the Democratic Republic of Congo, primarily through Uganda, according to recent findings highlighting the scale of illicit mineral trade in the
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 – Hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of gold extracted from Ituri Province is being illegally smuggled out of the Democratic Republic of Congo, primarily through Uganda, according to recent findings highlighting the scale of illicit mineral trade in the country's northeast.

The assessment estimates that gold production from a mining site between Mabanga and Nizi generated between US$300 million and US$800 million between March 2024 and March 2026. A second mining site near Yedi is reported to have produced more than two tonnes of gold since the beginning of 2025.

Despite this significant level of production, officially declared gold exports from Ituri totaled only 559 kilograms in 2025, revealing a substantial gap between estimated output and recorded exports.

The findings indicate that much of the undeclared gold is believed to be smuggled into neighboring Uganda. In 2025, Uganda recorded a historic 62 tonnes of gold exports valued at approximately US$6.4 billion, representing a 30 percent increase in export volume compared with the previous year. Analysts believe that a significant share of this increase is linked to gold originating from eastern DRC.

The report also highlights the rapid expansion of cyanide leaching operations used to process mining tailings in Djugu Territory. The practice is prohibited under Congolese law because of its environmental and safety risks, yet hundreds of tailings ponds have reportedly been established across the area.

Some of these mining sites are said to be under the influence of local armed groups, which allegedly impose taxes on mining activities, allowing them to generate revenue from the illicit exploitation of mineral resources.

The findings underscore the continuing challenges facing the DRC in regulating its mining sector, combating mineral smuggling, and preventing armed groups from financing their activities through the illegal exploitation of natural resources.

title: Paul Kagame nommé à la tête d'une commission mondiale de l'ONU sur l'IA
excerpt: Le président rwandais prend la présidence d'une nouvelle commission onusienne sur l'intelligence artificielle - un signal diplomatique fort.
title_en: President Kagame Named Chair of UN Global Commission on Artificial Intelligence
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda, July 7, 2026 - Rwandan President Paul Kagame has been appointed chair of the newly established United Nations AI for Good Global Commission, a high-level body tasked with promoting the responsible and inclusive development of artificial intelligence worldwide.
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda, July 7, 2026 - Rwandan President Paul Kagame has been appointed chair of the newly established United Nations AI for Good Global Commission, a high-level body tasked with promoting the responsible and inclusive development of artificial intelligence worldwide.

Kagame will lead the commission alongside Salesforce Chief Executive Marc Benioff, while International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Secretary-General Doreen Bogdan-Martin will serve as deputy chair. Supported by the ITU and UNESCO, the commission aims to reduce global technological disparities, promote international cooperation on AI, and help countries build capacity to harness emerging technologies.

The commission brings together more than 40 leaders from governments, international organizations, academia, and the technology industry, including executives from major global technology companies. Rather than developing binding regulations, it will focus on shaping global dialogue, promoting technical standards, and supporting AI adoption, particularly in developing countries.

Kagame's appointment reflects Rwanda's growing profile in digital innovation and technology policy. The country has expanded the use of artificial intelligence across sectors including healthcare, education, agriculture, justice, trade, and public services, while recently approving the creation of a national artificial intelligence agency to accelerate innovation, investment, and digital governance.

title: Tshisekedi ordonne la fin de la présence militaire illégale sur les sites miniers
excerpt: Le président congolaire exige le retrait immédiat des militaires des sites miniers - un signal fort pour la gouvernance des ressources.
title_en: Tshisekedi Orders End to Illegal Military Presence at Mining Sites to Strengthen Resource Governance
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 13, 2026 - President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi has ordered the immediate withdrawal of all military personnel and members of the Congolese National Police (PNC) illegally present at mining sites across the Democratic Republic of Congo, as part of efforts to improve
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 13, 2026 - President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi has ordered the immediate withdrawal of all military personnel and members of the Congolese National Police (PNC) illegally present at mining sites across the Democratic Republic of Congo, as part of efforts to improve transparency, security, and governance in the strategic mining sector.

Speaking during the 94th meeting of the Council of Ministers held on July 10, 2026, at the African Union City in Kinshasa, the Head of State reaffirmed the importance of mining resources for the country’s economic development while stressing the need to restore confidence among investors and international partners.

The DRC, which holds some of the world’s largest reserves of critical minerals essential for global energy transition technologies, has placed mining-sector reform at the center of its economic strategy. However, authorities continue to face challenges linked to illegal exploitation, weak oversight mechanisms, and interference by security forces in mining operations.

President Tshisekedi warned that the unauthorized presence of armed personnel at mining sites damages the country’s reputation, weakens state control, and encourages illegal activities that undermine responsible resource management.

According to the government, the involvement of uniformed personnel in mining areas contributes to intimidation, harassment, extortion, disruption of mineral traceability systems, and the development of smuggling networks.

The President stressed that security forces may only intervene in mining areas when their presence is legally authorized or officially requested by competent authorities. He rejected any occupation or interference that could compromise the rights of legitimate mining operators and local communities.

To enforce this decision, Félix Tshisekedi instructed several senior officials, including the Deputy Prime Minister in charge of Interior and Security, the Deputy Prime Minister responsible for Defense, the Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), and the Commissioner General of the Congolese National Police, to immediately implement measures aimed at eliminating illegal militarization of mining zones.

title_en: Seven Killed in Suspected ADF Attack on Outskirts of Beni
excerpt_en: Beni, North Kivu, July 14, 2026 – At least seven people, including four civilians and three soldiers, were killed in a predawn attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on the outskirts of Beni city in North Kivu, marking another deadly episode in the region's ongoi
body_en:
Beni, North Kivu, July 14, 2026 – At least seven people, including four civilians and three soldiers, were killed in a predawn attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on the outskirts of Beni city in North Kivu, marking another deadly episode in the region's ongoing insecurity.

The assault targeted the neighborhoods of Sayo and Matembo in Mulekera Commune during the early hours of Tuesday. According to local reports, four civilians were killed in the Mbutaba and Vuthala areas, where the attackers reportedly used bladed weapons during the assault. Several other civilians sustained injuries and were taken to nearby health facilities for treatment.

Local volunteers recovered the victims' bodies, which were later transferred to the morgue pending burial.

Community representatives credited the intervention of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) with preventing an even higher death toll, while urging residents to remain vigilant despite the heightened security response.

The attack also targeted security forces. According to security sources, government troops were caught in an ambush during the operation, resulting in the deaths of at least three soldiers.

The latest violence has triggered widespread panic across Sayo and neighboring communities. Fearing further attacks, many residents fled their homes, abandoning their belongings as they sought refuge in central Beni and other areas considered safer.

The incident highlights the persistent security challenges facing the Beni region, where repeated attacks by armed groups continue to cause civilian casualties, population displacement, and heightened humanitarian concerns.

body_en:
KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 5, 2026 - A United Nations panel of experts has reported that cooperation between the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) and the Wazalendo coalition has deepened in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with FDLR fighters now embedded within several Wazalendo armed groups operating in North Kivu Province.

According to the report, the collaboration extends across Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru, Walikale, Lubero, and Beni territories, where Wazalendo factions have conducted military operations independently and alongside the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC), particularly against AFC/M23 positions. The report states that some Wazalendo fighters have received specialized military training and have benefited from drone-supported operations.

The UN experts said FDLR combatants have been integrated into several Wazalendo groups, particularly those sharing anti-Tutsi ideology, including CMC/FDP, FDDP, and APCLS. The report argues that this cooperation has strengthened the FDLR while allowing it to evade international efforts calling for its dismantlement under the June 2025 Washington peace agreement.

The report further alleges that senior Congolese military officials were aware of the FDLR's presence within Wazalendo formations and that cooperation included intelligence sharing, logistical support, and weapons transfers. It also describes three regional Wazalendo coalitions operating across North Kivu and identifies two of them as hosting FDLR fighters. Additionally, the experts cite evidence of arms deliveries and continued coordination between FARDC officers and senior FDLR commanders, despite international commitments to dismantle the armed group.

title: Ndayishimiye intervient - l'opposition congolaise reporte ses manifestations
excerpt: La coalition C64 accepte un dialogue initié par le président burundais et reporte les manifestations anti-Tshisekedi prévues à Kinshasa.
title_en: Burundi’s Ndayishimiye Intervenes as Congolese Opposition Delays Anti-Tshisekedi Protests
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo's main opposition coalition, C64, has postponed planned protests demanding President Félix Tshisekedi’s resignation after accepting an invitation from Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye for talks on the country's po
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo's main opposition coalition, C64, has postponed planned protests demanding President Félix Tshisekedi’s resignation after accepting an invitation from Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye for talks on the country's political and security crisis.

The coalition, which brings together leading opposition figures including Martin Fayulu, Jean-Marc Kabund, Moïse Katumbi, Augustin Matata Ponyo and Delly Sesanga, announced on July 3 that it would attend an urgent meeting convened by Ndayishimiye in his capacity as Chairperson of the African Union. The discussions are expected to focus on security, political and institutional challenges facing the DRC.

According to sources in Kinshasa, Ndayishimiye, a close ally of President Tshisekedi, had encouraged dialogue between the government and opposition over the controversial plan to amend the Congolese Constitution, an initiative that has sparked growing political tensions.

The opposition had been preparing a major demonstration outside the Presidential Palace on July 8 to demand Tshisekedi's resignation, accusing him of attempting to undermine the Constitution. The planned protest followed earlier demonstrations on June 12 outside the National Assembly, where opposition supporters said they were dispersed by police and members of the ruling UDPS party's youth wing, Forces du Progrès.

The government has rejected the opposition's campaign. Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo recently suspended public demonstrations in Kinshasa, citing measures to prevent the spread of Ebola. Opposition leaders, however, argued that the decision was politically motivated, noting that Ebola cases have been concentrated in eastern provinces far from the capital.

Just a day before the postponement, Martin Fayulu had renewed calls for nationwide protests, urging Congolese citizens to demand Tshisekedi's resignation over what he described as attempts to violate the Constitution.

title: El Obeid - l'ONU alerte sur un risque de siège et une crise humanitaire

title_en: UN Warns El Obeid Could Face Siege as Humanitarian Crisis Deepens
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 – United Nations agencies have warned that the Sudanese city of El Obeid faces a growing risk of a major humanitarian catastrophe as escalating attacks, displacement, and restrictions on aid access raise fears of a crisis similar to previous sieges in Darfu
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 – United Nations agencies have warned that the Sudanese city of El Obeid faces a growing risk of a major humanitarian catastrophe as escalating attacks, displacement, and restrictions on aid access raise fears of a crisis similar to previous sieges in Darfur.

International officials said the strategic capital of North Kordofan State is facing increasing pressure as fighting intensifies around the city, with civilians suffering from shortages of essential services, including water and electricity.

The humanitarian situation across the Kordofan region has deteriorated sharply in recent months, with hundreds of thousands of people displaced by violence. Aid organizations reported a significant increase in displacement incidents, driven by attacks on communities and worsening insecurity.

An estimated 500,000 people remain trapped in El Obeid, where access to humanitarian assistance has become increasingly difficult. Repeated attacks on civilian infrastructure have disrupted basic services and left many residents struggling to obtain food, water, and medical care.

Humanitarian officials warned that continued inaction could lead to a repeat of the devastating events experienced in other besieged Sudanese cities, where civilians suffered widespread violence and displacement.

Aid agencies also highlighted growing challenges in maintaining relief operations due to declining resources and increased security risks. Emergency supplies, including food and shelter materials, are becoming increasingly limited as humanitarian needs continue to rise.

The warnings come after a humanitarian transport vehicle carrying vital relief supplies was destroyed in a drone strike in White Nile State. The shipment included essential items such as blankets, solar lamps, kitchen equipment, and other materials intended for conflict-affected communities.

title: Rwanda - 8 milliards de dollars d'investissements privés et 118 000 emplois attendus
excerpt: Kigali annonce près de 8 milliards de dollars de projets privés entre juin 2024 et juin 2026 - un levier majeur pour l'emploi.
title_en: Rwanda Attracts $8 Billion in Private Investment, Expected to Create 118,000 Jobs
excerpt_en: KIGALI, July 10, 2026 - Rwanda has registered nearly $8 billion in private investment projects between June 2024 and June 2026, with the investments expected to generate more than 118,000 jobs, Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva announced.
body_en:
KIGALI, July 10, 2026 - Rwanda has registered nearly $8 billion in private investment projects between June 2024 and June 2026, with the investments expected to generate more than 118,000 jobs, Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva announced.

The Prime Minister made the announcement on June 9, 2026, while presenting the government’s economic performance and measures to strengthen the country’s resilience amid domestic and global challenges before both chambers of Parliament.

Dr. Nsengiyumva said Rwanda’s economy continued to demonstrate strong growth, expanding by 10% in the first quarter of 2026, while more than 240,000 jobs have been created since the first quarter of 2025.

He said the country’s economic expansion has been accompanied by increased private sector investment, with major projects registered over the past two years.

“From 2024 to June this year, private investment projects worth nearly $8 billion were registered. It is expected that this investment will create 118,000 jobs,” he said.

The government has set a target of creating 250,000 jobs annually by 2029 as part of its long-term economic development strategy.

Rwanda’s gross domestic product (GDP) reached 6.346 trillion Rwandan francs in the first quarter of 2026, compared with 5.276 trillion Rwandan francs during the same period in 2025, representing a 10% increase.

The services sector remained the largest contributor to economic output, accounting for 52% of GDP, followed by industry at 24%, agriculture at 19%, and other sectors at 5%.

During the same period, agricultural production grew by 8%, industrial output increased by 13%, and services expanded by 7%.

Trade and commerce activity rose by 11%, while the transport sector also recorded 11% growth. Land transport increased by 10%, and air transport activity grew by 7%, reflecting continued expansion across key areas of the economy.

excerpt: La SAF annonce avoir repris Kurmuk - un point clé à la frontière, symbolique et logistique.
title_en: Sudanese Army Retakes Strategic Border Town of Kurmuk in Blue Nile
excerpt_en: KURMUK, July 8, 2026 - The Sudanese army has regained control of the strategic border town of Kurmuk in the Blue Nile region after intense clashes with forces from the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and a faction of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N) led by Abdel A
body_en:
KURMUK, July 8, 2026 - The Sudanese army has regained control of the strategic border town of Kurmuk in the Blue Nile region after intense clashes with forces from the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and a faction of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N) led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu.

The army’s advance ends months of control by the RSF and its allied fighters, who captured Kurmuk on March 24 during a major military operation in the border area near Ethiopia.

Sudanese authorities had previously accused Ethiopia of supporting the assault by allowing drone operations from Bahir Dar airport in the Amhara region. Ethiopian officials rejected the allegations.

The recapture was confirmed by Brigadier General Abadi al-Tahir, commander of the army’s Al-Naba al-Yaqeen task force, who said government forces had inflicted significant losses on opposing fighters and equipment, forcing surviving forces to withdraw.

The operation followed weeks of military movements by the army to secure areas surrounding Kurmuk and push RSF forces away from the strategic location.

Located near Sudan’s border with Ethiopia, Kurmuk has historically been a key battlefield due to its strategic importance. The town has repeatedly changed control during Sudan’s long-running conflicts, including the decades-long civil war between Khartoum and the SPLM under the leadership of the late John Garang.

title: Ouganda - la Haute Cour ordonne la présentation d'Erias Lukwago
excerpt: L'ancien maire de Kampala doit être présenté depuis la prison de Luzira dans le cadre d'une affaire liée à la trahison.
title_en: High Court Orders Production of Erias Lukwago for Treason-Related Trial
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The High Court in Kampala has ordered authorities at Luzira Upper Prison to produce former Kampala Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago in court next week as he faces charges of misprision of treason.
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The High Court in Kampala has ordered authorities at Luzira Upper Prison to produce former Kampala Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago in court next week as he faces charges of misprision of treason.

A production warrant issued by the High Court Criminal Division on July 16 directs Luzira Upper Prison authorities to present Lukwago before Justice David Matovu on July 24, 2026, at 10:00am.

The warrant was issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. HCT-00-CR-CM-0261-2026, where Lukwago is listed as the applicant and the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) as the respondent.

The Officer in Charge of Luzira Upper Prison has been instructed to ensure Lukwago’s attendance before the court on the scheduled date.

The development followed a decision by Makindye Chief Magistrate Sarah Basemera to commit Lukwago to the High Court for trial over charges of misprision of treason.

Prosecution alleges that Lukwago, who also leads the People’s Front for Freedom (PFF), failed to report information about an alleged plan to overthrow the government by force of arms despite allegedly being aware of the plot.

The state claims the alleged offence occurred between January and June 2026.

Lukwago has denied the allegations, maintaining his innocence.

The case will now proceed before the High Court, where further guidance on the trial process is expected during the July 24 hearing.

title_en: Uganda Energy Ministry Launches Reforms to Drive $500 Billion Economy Vision by 2040
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 – The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development has launched a leadership retreat aimed at transforming the energy and minerals sector into a major engine of industrialisation, job creation, and economic growth as Uganda pursues its target of a US$
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 – The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development has launched a leadership retreat aimed at transforming the energy and minerals sector into a major engine of industrialisation, job creation, and economic growth as Uganda pursues its target of a US$500 billion economy by 2040.

The five-day retreat, held in Kampala, brings together senior ministry officials, government agencies, state corporations, and technical experts to develop reforms focused on expanding energy access, promoting mineral value addition, strengthening industrial capacity, and improving coordination across the sector.

Energy and Mineral Development Minister Dr Monica Musenero urged ministry leaders to move beyond routine administration and reposition the sector as a strategic driver of national transformation.

She introduced the One MEMD Doctrine, an institutional framework designed to align departments and agencies under a common vision focused on using energy, minerals, and natural resources to create wealth and support industrial development.

Musenero said Uganda must shift from exporting raw materials to building domestic processing industries that increase value, create jobs, and strengthen national revenues.

She emphasized that natural resources should not only be viewed as commodities for extraction but as foundations for innovation, manufacturing, and long-term economic growth.

The government estimates Uganda’s economy at more than US$60 billion and aims to expand it to US$500 billion by 2040 through industrialisation, science, technology, innovation, and increased private sector participation.

The energy and minerals sector is expected to play a central role in achieving this ambition through developments in oil production, mineral exploitation, electricity generation, and expansion of energy infrastructure.

excerpt: Quatre suspects arrêtés à Lira après la saisie de billets américains contrefaits d'une valeur alléguée de 9 millions de dollars.
title_en: Ugandan Police Dismantle Suspected Counterfeit Currency Ring, Seize Alleged $9 Million in Fake Notes
excerpt_en: Lira, Uganda, July 2, 2026 – Ugandan authorities have arrested four suspects following the seizure of United States dollar notes with a purported face value of USD 9 million during an intelligence-led operation targeting a suspected counterfeit currency network in Lira City.
body_en:
Lira, Uganda, July 2, 2026 – Ugandan authorities have arrested four suspects following the seizure of United States dollar notes with a purported face value of USD 9 million during an intelligence-led operation targeting a suspected counterfeit currency network in Lira City.

The operation was conducted in Ireda Shamba Cell, Lira City East Division, after investigators received information that counterfeit currency and related materials were being stored at a private residence. A lawful search of the property led to the discovery of a safe believed to contain the suspected counterfeit notes.

During the operation, officers recovered approximately 100 bundles of USD 100 notes suspected to be counterfeit, along with several motor vehicle logbooks and additional United States dollar notes in various denominations.

Preliminary investigations indicate that the safe had been delivered to the residence by one of the suspects, who is already facing separate allegations of obtaining money by false pretences. Authorities also believe the suspects may have been involved in similar activities over an extended period, with possible links to associates operating in Soroti City.

The recovered currency has been secured as evidence and will undergo forensic examination to determine its authenticity. Investigators are working to establish the full extent of the suspected network and identify any additional individuals connected to the operation.

Authorities said investigations remain ongoing and that further arrests are expected as efforts continue to dismantle the alleged counterfeit currency network.

title: Museveni - croissance industrielle liée aux marchés garantis et à la production locale
excerpt: Le président ougandais insiste : sans débouchés fiables, pas d'industrialisation durable - priorité aux marchés et au made in Uganda.
title_en: Museveni Links Uganda’s Industrial Growth to Reliable Markets and Local Production
excerpt_en: KISOZI, July 16, 2026 - President Yoweri Museveni has said guaranteed markets are essential for expanding production and accelerating Uganda’s industrial growth, arguing that farmers can supply agro-processing industries if they are assured of stable demand.
body_en:
KISOZI, July 16, 2026 - President Yoweri Museveni has said guaranteed markets are essential for expanding production and accelerating Uganda’s industrial growth, arguing that farmers can supply agro-processing industries if they are assured of stable demand.

Speaking during the commissioning of the National Enterprise Corporation (NEC) Meat and Beans Processing Plant in Kisozi, Gomba District, Museveni described the facility as a major step in Uganda’s industrialisation agenda, promoting value addition and strategic self-reliance.

The plant, established through a partnership between NEC and businessman Francis Ragwa, will process canned beef and beans for domestic consumption and export markets.

Museveni said Uganda already possesses the production capacity needed to support the facility but noted that the key challenge has been organising farmers and creating reliable markets for their products.

He pointed to the growth of the coffee and dairy sectors as examples of how market-driven production can transform industries and improve economic opportunities.

“Once I am sure about the market, I can mobilise Ugandans to produce because the economics are correct. The stimulus for production is the market,” Museveni said.

The President highlighted Uganda’s expanding cattle population, which has grown from about three million in 1986 to more than 16 million, as evidence of the country’s ability to support a thriving meat-processing industry through both commercial and small-scale farmers.

He urged stakeholders to develop effective production models that ensure farmers directly benefit from value addition opportunities.

Museveni also praised NEC and its partners for completing the project despite challenges, including delays linked to the Covid-19 pandemic.

Minister of Defence and Veteran Affairs Kiryowa Kiwanuka described the facility as an important milestone in Uganda’s pursuit of industrialisation and self-sufficiency. He said the country has historically relied on imported operational rations, including canned beef and beans, but the new plant would help reduce that dependence.
